messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: Old inla code running very slow now
parts:
Hi all,

I hope this question is not too vague. I have been trying to rerun an inla model I first developed 3 or 4 years ago. I haven't changed any of the R script code or inla model specification. I am on a new hexcore macbook vs my old quad core one. Because its anew machine I also reinstalled software so I'm on newer versions of MacOS (Mojave), R (3.5.1), BLAS, (Current stable release installed today), etc. I have mostly been doing other work and so I've not been keeping up with the developments in INLA - I'm conscious many things could have changed that I'm unaware of.

My model has quite a large graph - about 55,000 nodes. Previously it run in about 15-16 minutes using the same data. Now, R code runs fine, inla appears to start fine, producing the messages below. However, the model is taking along time to run (45mins and counting).

My model code is:
# Define INLA formulae
formula.allcases = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph="nb.sa.txt",
                                 hyper = list(prec.unstruct = list(param = c(1,0.0001)),
                                              prec.spatial = list(param=c(1,0.1))))

mod1 <- inla(formula.allcases, data=data1, family="poisson", E = exTOT,
                     control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1, cdf=c(0)),
                     control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

When I run it the console returns the messages below, however after 45 mins and counting I'm still waiting.

Can anyone advise what I should be looking at to speed things up? I will let it continue to run so long as I don't need to do something else in the mean time to see if it comes back with errors.

Thanks,
James

On Wednesday, January 9, 2019 at 5:04:56 PM UTC, jpkrooney wrote:
Hi all,

I hope this question is not too vague. I have been trying to rerun an inla model I first developed 3 or 4 years ago. I haven't changed any of the R script code or inla model specification. I am on a new hexcore macbook vs my old quad core one. Because its anew machine I also reinstalled software so I'm on newer versions of MacOS (Mojave), R (3.5.1), BLAS, (Current stable release installed today), etc. I have mostly been doing other work and so I've not been keeping up with the developments in INLA - I'm conscious many things could have changed that I'm unaware of.

My model has quite a large graph - about 55,000 nodes. Previously it run in about 15-16 minutes using the same data. Now, R code runs fine, inla appears to start fine, producing the messages below. However, the model is taking along time to run (45mins and counting).

My model code is:
# Define INLA formulae
formula.allcases = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph="nb.sa.txt",
                                 hyper = list(prec.unstruct = list(param = c(1,0.0001)),
                                              prec.spatial = list(param=c(1,0.1))))

mod1 <- inla(formula.allcases, data=data1, family="poisson", E = exTOT,
                     control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1, cdf=c(0)),
                     control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

When I run it the console returns the messages below, however after 45 mins and counting I'm still waiting.

Can anyone advise what I should be looking at to speed things up? I will let it continue to run so long as I don't need to do something else in the mean time to see if it comes back with errors.

Thanks,
James

It could very well be (thx Finn!) that the default integration scheme
for |theta| = 2, was at some point changed from "ccd" to "grid".
looking back, it was here:

changeset: 3172:4fae4c750a63
user: Havard Rue <havar...@math.ntnu.no>
date: Mon Mar 14 09:19:35 2016 +0100
files: gmrflib/approx-inference.c
description:
Set int.strategy = auto to grid also for nhyper=2

and it might very well be this.

you can check it by 'reverting' back to the old style using argument

control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd")

you can also check if the new testing version runs better after setting

inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE)

(assuming you're on R-3.5)

let me know.

Best
H

Hi Havard,

That worked thanks you. The ccd integration strategy brought the runtime down to about 10 mins. The mkl option by itself didn't seem to make much difference (at least I didn't have patient to wait for it to finish so it may have been a bit quicker but not dramatically. Doing both options together seemed to improve things a bit more taking about 9 mins.

Thanks for your help!
On Wednesday, January 9, 2019 at 7:52:43 PM UTC, Helpdesk wrote:

It could very well be (thx Finn!) that the default integration scheme
for |theta| = 2, was at some point changed from "ccd" to "grid".
looking back, it was here:

changeset:   3172:4fae4c750a63
user:        Havard Rue <havar...@math.ntnu.no>
date:        Mon Mar 14 09:19:35 2016 +0100
files:       gmrflib/approx-inference.c
description:
Set int.strategy = auto to grid also for nhyper=2

and it might very well be this.

you can check it by 'reverting' back to the old style using argument

control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd")

you can also check if the new testing version runs better after setting

inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE)

(assuming you're on R-3.5)

let me know.

Best
H
